note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A farmer in St Elizabeth brings in a trailer with a cracked drawbar. What should you do first?
options: Weld over the crack at once to save the farmer some time
Inspect the whole drawbar and find out why it failed
Cut the drawbar off and weld on any spare length of tube
Grind the crack out and paint it so it looks like new

questions.stem: Which is usually the strongest reason to replace a part rather than repair it?
options: The customer would like it painted in a new colour
The welder has plenty of spare time this week
The part is mild steel, which is easy to weld
Rust has thinned it below a safe strength

questions.stem: A modification will change the way a load-bearing platform frame carries its load. Who should approve it before work starts?
options: A qualified engineer or the person responsible
The welder who happens to be on shift that day
The driver who delivered the frame to the shop
Any trainee who has read the original drawing

questions.stem: There is no drawing for a broken bracket. Why should you identify its material before repairing it?
options: So you can charge more for a special material
So the bracket can be painted in the right colour afterwards
So you choose the right filler, preheat and method
So the welding machine can be switched to AC

questions.stem: A magnet does not stick to a tank fitting that looks like steel. What is it most likely made of?
options: Plain mild steel
Grey cast iron
Austenitic stainless or a non-ferrous metal
High carbon tool steel

questions.stem: A drum that held fuel needs a bracket welded onto it. What must happen first?
options: It is cleaned and proved gas-free by a competent person
It is rinsed out once with water and welded at once
It is left open in the sun for an hour before welding
It is welded on low current so no sparks get inside

questions.stem: You must repair the guard on a machine in the Centre's workshop. What must be done before you start?
options: Leave the machine running so you can see how the guard fits
Ask a trainee to stand by the stop button while you work
Switch the machine off at its own switch, then begin
Isolate and lock off the machine and tag it, as the rules say

questions.stem: Before cutting out a damaged length of column in a steel frame, what must be in place?
options: A fresh coat of primer on the column above the cut
Temporary props that carry the load safely
A new drawing of the frame printed full size
A second welder ready to weld the moment it is cut

questions.stem: Before a crack is gouged out, why is dye penetrant used along it?
options: To cool the steel so the crack closes up
To clean off paint and rust in one step
To make the crack weld more easily later
To find exactly where the crack ends

questions.stem: Why is a crack removed down to sound metal before it is welded?
options: So the repair needs less filler metal overall
A crack left under the weld can grow again
So the finished weld looks flatter and neater
So the inspector has a groove to measure later

questions.stem: Some repair procedures ask for a small hole to be drilled just past each end of a crack. Why?
options: To let welding gas escape from inside the plate
To mark the crack for the painter to find later
To stop the crack running further during repair
To fit bolts that hold the two sides together

questions.stem: Which is usually the best way to remove an old fillet weld so a damaged bracket can come off without much harm to the main plate?
options: Air carbon arc gouging or grinding, then dressing
Hammering the bracket until the weld snaps
Heating the whole plate red hot and pulling it off
Drilling a row of holes through the main plate

questions.stem: A long side rail on a truck body needs a 1 m repair weld. Which method helps control distortion?
options: Short welds placed in a balanced, staggered order
One long continuous run at the highest current setting
The full length from one side in a single pass
Heat the rail red hot first, then weld it fast

questions.stem: You must weld a repair on a galvanised gate. What should be done before welding?
options: Weld through the zinc to save time preparing it
Paint over the zinc so that it does not burn off
Remove the zinc near the joint; use fume extraction
Dip the joint in water so the zinc stays cool

questions.stem: After a galvanised part has been repaired by welding, how is the bare area protected?
options: It is left bare, as weld metal does not rust
With zinc-rich paint or the method specified
It is oiled once and then left to dry off
A coat of ordinary household gloss paint

questions.stem: Why is a broken cast iron part often preheated and welded in short runs?
options: So the casting turns into mild steel
So any electrode at all can be used
So it becomes harder to machine later
So it is less likely to crack from stress

questions.stem: The cutting edge of a loader bucket is badly worn. Which repair builds it up so it resists wear?
options: Painting it with a thick coat of bitumen paint
Hardfacing it with a wear-resistant filler
Bolting on a sheet of thin aluminium
Welding a pattern of mild steel tacks

questions.stem: You must make a new part to replace a broken one, and there is no drawing. How do you make sure it will fit?
options: Make it a little smaller so it is easy to fit
Copy the broken part by eye and trim it on site
Ask the customer what size they think it was
Measure the old part and its fixing points, sketch, check

questions.stem: A customer asks you to add a loading ramp to a trailer. Why should you check the trailer's load and balance before agreeing?
options: The change could overload or unbalance it
Ramps must always be made of stainless steel
Only the customer is allowed to weld on ramps
It means you will not need to give a price

questions.stem: When a modification is finished, why should the drawings be marked up to show the change?
options: So the customer can ask for a refund later
So someone else can price the job again
So later repairs work from what was built
So it looks the same as the first drawing

questions.stem: How should you choose the filler metal for a repair weld on a steel part?
options: Use whatever electrode is in the holder already
Always use the thickest electrode in the store
Match the parent metal, as the WPS or maker says
Use stainless filler on every repair, to be safe

questions.stem: Why might a repair on a thick, high-strength steel part need preheat?
options: To slow cooling and lower the risk of cracking
To make the steel soft enough to bend by hand
To burn off the paint so no cleaning is needed
To let the welder work faster and charge less

questions.stem: Why are tacks and clamps used to hold a replacement section before it is fully welded?
options: So the section can be painted before welding
So the inspector can sign off the job early
So the full weld can be done with no fit-up
So its alignment is checked and set right first

questions.stem: After a crack in a steel bracket has been repaired, which is a good check for any surface crack left?
options: Tapping it with a hammer and listening to it
Dye penetrant or magnetic particle test
Weighing it against the old bracket
Painting it and watching for bubbles

questions.stem: A repaired lifting beam is ready to go back into service. Who decides whether it may be used?
options: The welder, once the weld looks neat enough
The customer, as soon as the bill is paid
The driver who will move the beam about
A competent person, after inspection and test

questions.stem: Why should you take photos before, during and after a repair?
options: So they can be posted on social media
They show the damage, the work and the result
So the customer can be charged a higher price
So no written report has to be made later

questions.stem: Which details should a repair report include?
options: Only the welder's name and the date of the job
Only the price charged and how it was paid
Damage found, method, materials and checks
Only the colour of paint used to finish it

questions.stem: A repair would cost nearly as much as a new part, and the part would still be weak. What should you advise?
options: Replace it, and explain why to the customer
Repair it anyway, as repairs earn more money
Do half the repair now and the rest next year
Weld a plate on top and charge for a new part

questions.stem: How do you find out how much sound metal is left in a rusted leg of a water tank stand?
options: Clean back to bright metal and measure it
Paint over the rust and judge by the colour
Hit it hard with a hammer to see if it bends
Work it out from the age of the tank stand

questions.stem: Why must old paint be removed from the area before a repair is welded?
options: Old paint makes the steel heavier to lift
Paint makes the weld bead come out shiny
It gives off harmful fume and spoils the weld
Paint stops the welding machine from working

questions.stem: Why should the cut lines be marked before a damaged section of a frame is cut out?
options: So the offcut sells for more as scrap metal
So only the damage is removed and the new piece fits
So the cutting torch uses less oxygen on the job
So the customer can sign each line before cutting

questions.stem: You will weld a repair inside a hardware store. Which fire precautions are needed?
options: Weld quickly and leave as soon as you have finished
Ask the shop staff to keep an eye on it while they work
Wet the area with a hose and weld while it is still wet
Clear flammables, screen off, extinguisher and fire watch

questions.stem: A repaired frame has pulled out of square. What is a suitable way to correct it?
options: Leave it, as the customer will not notice it
Controlled heat or pulling, then check again
Cut out every weld and build the frame again
Hammer it cold until it looks about straight

questions.stem: Why is it good practice to write a short repair procedure before a larger repair?
options: So the job takes longer and earns more
So the customer can then do it alone
So no one has to inspect the work later
So steps, checks and safety are agreed

questions.stem: A broken 12 mm flat bar must be joined with a full-strength butt weld. How should the ends be prepared?
options: Bevel them to suit the WPS and set the gap
Butt them tight together with no bevel at all
Overlap them by 50 mm and weld round the edge
Grind both ends round and fill the gap with weld

questions.stem: A repair adds a reinforcing plate to a beam. Why are its corners rounded, with welds not stopped at sharp corners?
options: To make the plate easier to paint later on
To use less filler metal on the whole job
To avoid stress points where cracks start
To let rain drain away from under the plate

questions.stem: A pin hole in a trailer hinge has worn oval. Which repair restores it best?
options: Fill it with body filler and drill it again
Weld a large washer over it on one side
Build it up with weld, then bore it true
Fit a bigger pin and leave the hole oval

questions.stem: During a repair you find more damage than you quoted for. What should you do?
options: Stop, tell the customer and agree the extra
Fix it quietly and add it to the final bill
Leave it and finish only what was quoted
Paint over it so that nobody can see it

questions.stem: A customer asks you to weld a patch on a cracked compressed-air tank. What should you do?
options: Weld it at once, as air is not dangerous
Patch it with a plate and fill it with water
Grind out the crack and paint over it
Decline unless approved people repair it to code

questions.stem: As team leader on a repair, what is the best way to brief two trainees before they start?
options: Tell them to watch you closely and not ask anything
Go over the procedure, hazards and their tasks
Hand them the job card and leave the shop
Let them work it out as they go along

questions.stem: A frame is made of 50 × 50 × 3 SHS. Which piece should be used for a replacement section?
options: 50 × 50 × 2 SHS, as it is lighter to carry
40 × 40 × 3 SHS, as it is easier to weld in
Round tube of about the same weight per metre
The same 50 × 50 × 3 SHS, unless approved

questions.stem: Why is the area around a damaged part checked for other damage before the repair starts?
options: To find more work to bill the customer for
Hidden damage may need repairing as well
So the welder can rest before starting
Because the drawings must all be redrawn

questions.stem: After the repair, what should be done with the old damaged parts and offcuts?
options: Leave them on the floor for the cleaner
Put them in the stock rack to use again
Label any to keep, and scrap the rest safely
Throw them over the fence behind the shop

questions.stem: Why must the protective coating be restored after a repair on outdoor steelwork?
options: Bare weld areas rust quickly outdoors
Fresh paint makes the weld much stronger
The inspector will not look at painted welds
Paint stops the part from distorting later

questions.stem: A repaired gate hinge must be checked before handover. What is the best check?
options: Swing the gate fully; check line and weld
Look at it from a distance and sign it off
Paint it and wait for the customer to complain
Hang a heavy load on it until something bends

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In penetrant testing, what is the name of the white spray that draws the dye back out of a crack so it can be seen?
What name is given to a weld deposit laid on a surface to make it resist wear?
What term means the original metal of the part being repaired, as opposed to the weld metal?
What written document records the damage found, the repair method, the materials used and the checks made?
What is the name of the short tube pressed into a worn hole to bring it back to size?
What word describes a repair in which a damaged length of section is cut out and a new length is welded in its place?
What name is given to welding short lengths in the opposite direction to the overall progress of the weld, to reduce distortion?
What test identifies a type of steel by the colour and shape of the sparks from a grinder?
Which metal is most often used in electrodes for welding repairs on cast iron?
What written document gives permission to weld or cut in an area where there is a fire risk?
Breathing fume from welding galvanised steel can cause metal fume fever. Which metal in the coating gives off this fume?
What do we call drawings that are corrected after a job to show how it was actually built?
A repair takes 6 hours of labour at J$2,500 an hour, plus J$9,000 of materials. What is the total cost before GCT, in J$?
What name is given to the softer weld layer laid first under a hardfacing deposit, to help it bond to the part?
What do we call checking a repair with the eyes, a torch, a mirror and weld gauges, with no special test equipment?

essays.stem: A school in May Pen reports a cracked steel stair stringer. Describe how you would assess the damage and decide whether to repair or replace the stringer.
essays.modelAnswer: First I make the stair safe by closing it off so nobody uses it. I look at the drawings if there are any, and ask how and when the crack was found. I clean the area back to bright metal and inspect the whole stringer, the treads and the fixings, not just the crack. I use dye penetrant to find the full length of the crack and look for others. I measure how much sound metal is left where there is rust, and check the stair for bending or movement. I try to find the cause, such as a poor weld, overloading, rust or vibration, because the repair must remove the cause too. I identify the material. Then I compare repair and replacement: the strength after repair, the cost, the time and how long each will last. If the stringer is badly rusted or the crack is long, I would replace it. A load-bearing repair is agreed with the engineer or person responsible before work starts.
markingPoints: Makes the stair safe and closed to users
Cleans and inspects the whole stringer, using dye penetrant to find the crack's extent
Finds the cause of the failure and identifies the material
Compares repair and replacement on strength, cost, time and life
Gets approval from the engineer or person responsible

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would repair a crack in a welded steel bracket that carries a load.
essays.modelAnswer: I take the load off the bracket or support it with props, and get any approval needed. I clean the area to bright metal and use dye penetrant to find both ends of the crack, marking them. If the procedure asks, I drill a small hole just past each end so the crack cannot run. I identify the material and choose the filler and any preheat from the WPS or the maker's guidance. I remove the crack completely by grinding or air carbon arc gouging, shaped like a U or V groove, and check with dye penetrant that no crack is left. I preheat if required, then weld the groove in runs, cleaning each one, and keep the heat even to control distortion. I dress the weld smooth with no sharp notches. When it is cool, I inspect it visually and with dye penetrant, record the work, and restore the paint before the bracket goes back into use.
markingPoints: Supports or unloads the bracket and gets approval
Finds and marks the crack ends; stop holes if the procedure asks
Removes the crack fully to sound metal and checks it
Chooses filler and preheat from the WPS and welds in clean runs
Inspects with dye penetrant, records and restores the coating

essays.stem: Explain the safety steps needed before a fabrication is repaired where it stands, on a plant or a building site.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with a risk assessment and the site's permits. If the item is part of a machine or plant, it is isolated, locked off and tagged by the right people, and stored energy such as springs, hydraulics or air is released. If there is fire risk, a hot-work permit is issued; flammable materials are moved or covered, screens are set up, an extinguisher is ready and a fire watch stays during and after the work. Any tank, drum or pipe that has held fuel or chemicals must be cleaned and proved gas-free by a competent person before any heat is applied. If a load-bearing part is to be cut, the structure is propped first so nothing can fall or move. Access at height is by a tagged scaffold or proper platform. I check the ventilation and fume extraction, especially for paint, zinc or confined spaces. Finally I brief the team and set up barriers so the public stays clear.
markingPoints: Risk assessment; isolation, lock-off and tag of plant; stored energy released
Hot-work permit, fire precautions and fire watch
Tanks and drums cleaned and proved gas-free before heat
Props load-bearing parts before cutting; safe access at height
Ventilation, barriers and a team briefing

essays.stem: A customer wants a hinged door added to an existing steel security grille. Explain how you would plan, carry out and control this modification.
essays.modelAnswer: I visit the site and measure the grille, the opening and the wall fixings, and talk to the customer about the size, the lock and how the door should swing. I check that cutting an opening will not weaken the grille or its fixings, and that the frame can carry the weight of the door. I make a sketch or drawing of the change, with the door frame, hinges, lock plate and any extra bars, and agree it and the price with the customer. In the shop I make the door and frame to the drawing and check them for square. On site I mark the opening, support the grille, cut out the bars, fit a strong frame round the opening and weld the hinges so the door hangs true and swings freely. I fit the lock and check it. I clean the welds and restore the paint. Finally I mark up the drawing as built, record the job and show the customer how the door works.
markingPoints: Measures and agrees the change with the customer
Checks the grille and fixings will stay strong; drawing or sketch made
Makes the door and frame to the drawing and checks square
Supports, cuts, frames and hangs the door correctly, with the lock working
Restores the finish, marks up as built and hands over

essays.stem: Describe how you would cut out and replace a badly rusted section of one leg of a steel water tank stand.
essays.modelAnswer: The tank is emptied, or the stand is propped, so that the leg carries no load during the work, and the job is approved by the person responsible. I clean the leg and measure the steel to find where the sound metal starts above and below the rust. I mark square cut lines in sound metal and cut out the rusted section with a grinder or torch. I get a new piece of the same section and grade, or as approved, and cut it to fit with the ends prepared for full-strength butt welds as the WPS says. I clamp and tack it in, checking that it lines up with the leg in both directions and that the leg is plumb. I weld it fully, cleaning each run, and in a sequence that keeps the leg straight. I inspect the welds, then remove the props slowly. Finally I restore the coating and record the repair.
markingPoints: Unloads or props the stand and gets approval
Finds sound metal and marks square cut lines
Uses matching section with butt-weld preparation to the WPS
Tacks, checks alignment and plumb, welds in sequence
Inspects, removes props carefully, restores coating and records

essays.stem: Explain why repair welds often cause distortion, and describe how you would prevent and correct it on a repaired steel frame.
essays.modelAnswer: When a weld is made, the weld and the metal beside it expand with the heat and then shrink as they cool. The shrinkage pulls the parts towards the weld, so a frame can bend, twist or pull out of square. Repairs are often made on one side of a part, or on a frame that is already held in place, which makes the pull worse and can also build up stress. To prevent it, I clamp or brace the frame, tack evenly, and use the smallest weld that the job needs. I balance the welding on both sides of a joint, use short runs, back-step or skip welding, and let the work cool between runs. Before welding I can also preset the parts slightly in the opposite direction. If the frame still distorts, I measure the diagonals and straightness, then correct it with controlled heat, using small heated spots, or by pulling with clamps, and check it again.
markingPoints: Explains expansion and shrinkage as the cause
Clamps, braces and tacks evenly before welding
Uses the smallest weld, balanced sequence and short or back-step runs
Presets parts to allow for shrinkage
Measures and corrects with controlled heat or pulling, and rechecks

essays.stem: Compare the precautions for repairing three items: a galvanised gate, a cast iron pump bracket and a worn loader bucket edge.
essays.modelAnswer: For the galvanised gate, the zinc is ground off for a short distance around the joint before welding, because zinc spoils the weld and its fume can cause metal fume fever. I use fume extraction and a suitable respirator, and afterwards I restore the protection with zinc-rich paint or the method specified. For the cast iron bracket, the material is brittle and cracks easily from heat stress. I clean it well, often preheat it evenly, use nickel electrodes or the filler the procedure gives, weld short runs, peen each one lightly while hot if the procedure says, and let it cool slowly, wrapped up. For the worn bucket edge, I clean it and check the base steel, then build it up with a buffer layer if needed and finish with hardfacing filler laid in the pattern the maker advises. Hardfacing is hard and may crack across, which can be normal for some fillers. In each case I follow the maker's instructions.
markingPoints: Galvanised: remove zinc, fume control, restore zinc protection
Cast iron: preheat, nickel filler, short runs and slow cooling
Bucket: clean, buffer layer if needed, hardfacing filler
Gives a reason for each precaution
Refers to the maker's instructions or the procedure

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect a finished repair and what you would record before the item is handed back.
essays.modelAnswer: When the repair has cooled, I inspect it visually with good light, a mirror and weld gauges. I check the weld size and profile against the drawing or procedure, and look for cracks, undercut, porosity, lack of fusion and spatter. For cracks I use dye penetrant, or magnetic particle testing if it is available and required. I check the dimensions, alignment and squareness of the repaired item and that moving parts work freely. If the item lifts or carries a load, a competent person decides whether a load test is needed before it is used. I write a repair report with the customer, the item, the damage found and its likely cause, the method, the materials and filler, the welder, the inspection results and any advice, such as a date to inspect again. I attach photos taken before, during and after. Copies go to the customer and the job file.
markingPoints: Visual inspection of size, profile and defects with gauges
Surface crack test such as dye penetrant where needed
Checks dimensions, alignment and function; load test by a competent person if needed
Writes a repair report with damage, cause, method, materials and results
Adds photos and gives copies to the customer and the file

essays.stem: Explain how you would deal with a customer from the first inspection of a damaged item to handing back the repaired item.
essays.modelAnswer: At the first visit I listen to the customer, ask how the damage happened and look at the item with them. I explain in plain words what I found, the choices of repair or replacement, and my advice, with the reasons. I give a written quotation with the work, price in J$, GCT at the current rate and the time it will take, and get their agreement before starting. If I find more damage during the job, I stop and tell the customer, explain the extra work and cost and get their agreement before carrying on. I keep them informed of the progress. At handover I show them the repaired item, explain what was done, give them the repair report and any care advice, such as painting or checking it again in six months. I make sure the invoice matches what was agreed, and ask if they are satisfied.
markingPoints: Listens, inspects with the customer and explains the options and advice
Gives a clear written quotation and gets agreement
Stops and agrees any extra work found
Keeps the customer informed
Hands over with an explanation, report, care advice and a matching invoice

essays.stem: You lead three trainees repairing a farm trailer with a bent cross member and a cracked spring hanger. Explain how you would plan the job and lead the team.
essays.modelAnswer: I inspect the trailer with the team, decide the repairs and write a short procedure: support the trailer on stands, remove the wheels if needed, straighten or replace the cross member, and remove and replace or repair the spring hanger. I list the materials and tools and check they are ready. I brief the team on the hazards: the trailer must sit on proper stands, never on a jack alone, fire precautions for hot work, PPE, and fume from old paint. I give each person a task, for example one cleaning and preparing, one cutting and fitting, one welding under my eye, and rotate the tasks so all learn. I set check points where I inspect the fit-up and the welds before the next step. I check alignment of the axle and springs before final welding. At the end I make sure the trailer is inspected, painted, and recorded, the area is cleaned, and I review the job with the team.
markingPoints: Inspects and writes a procedure, with materials and tools ready
Briefs hazards, including safe support on stands and hot work
Gives and rotates clear tasks
Inspects at check points, including axle alignment
Ensures inspection, finishing, records, clean-up and a team review

practical1.title: Assess and repair cracked welded brackets, with crack testing and a repair report
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group two or three welded steel brackets, each with a crack or a cut that stands in for a crack (prepared by the assessor). As a group, inspect each bracket, clean the area and use dye penetrant to find and mark the ends of each crack. Decide whether each bracket should be repaired or replaced, and write a short repair procedure for the ones you will repair: how the crack is removed, the joint shape, the filler, any preheat and the checks. Each member then takes part in a repair: removing the crack completely by grinding or gouging to sound metal (checked again with dye penetrant), welding the groove in clean runs and dressing the weld. While one member works, another acts as inspector and records the steps. When cool, inspect each repair visually and with dye penetrant, and complete a repair report with before, during and after photos. Photograph each stage and add the photos, the procedure and the report to the group's practical.
materials: Two or three welded steel brackets with cracks or crack-like cuts, prepared by the assessor
Dye penetrant kit (cleaner, penetrant, developer) and rags
Angle grinders with grinding and flap discs, and gouging equipment if the Centre allows
MMAW or GMAW welding set, with the filler given in the procedure
Weld gauges, torch, mirror, temperature crayon
Repair procedure sheet and repair report sheet
photos: Each bracket before work, with the crack marked
Dye penetrant showing the crack ends
The crack removed, with the clean groove checked by dye penetrant
A member welding the repair in full PPE
The final dye penetrant check on the repair
The completed repair report and the cleaned work area
checklist: Inspected the bracket and found the crack ends correctly with dye penetrant
Took part in a sound repair-or-replace decision and the written procedure
Removed the crack fully to sound metal and checked it before welding
Welded the groove in clean runs with the right filler and settings
Dressed the weld smoothly with no sharp notches
Inspected the repair and recorded the results accurately
Wore the right PPE and followed the SDS for the dye penetrant
Left the area clean, with waste and aerosol cans disposed of correctly
safety: Use dye penetrant sprays in a ventilated area away from arcs and sparks; read the SDS
Wear a face shield and hearing protection when grinding, and full welding PPE when welding
Weld only in booths or behind screens; keep flammables away and an extinguisher ready
Treat repaired brackets as hot; use tongs and mark them HOT
Use fume extraction when welding over any old paint residue

practical2.title: Cut out and replace a damaged member of a steel frame, then modify the frame to a marked-up drawing
practical2.brief: The assessor gives your group a small welded steel frame (for example a gate frame or bench frame) with one bent or rusted member, and a drawing marked up with a modification, such as a new hinge lug and a latch plate. As a group, inspect the frame, measure it, and record its diagonals and straightness. Plan the work: which member is cut out, where the cut lines go, the replacement section, the joint preparation, the welding order to control distortion, and each member's task. Mark the cut lines, support the frame and cut out the damaged member. Prepare and fit a new length of the same section, tack it and check that the frame is square and flat before full welding. Then make and fit the parts for the modification as the marked-up drawing shows. Weld in the planned order, check the frame again and correct any distortion. Clean the welds, prime the repaired areas, and mark up the drawing as built. Every member cuts, fits or welds at least one part and records at least one check. Photograph each stage and add the photos, the plan and the as-built drawing to the group's practical.
materials: A small welded steel frame with one damaged member, and a marked-up drawing from the assessor
Replacement section to match the frame, and flat bar or plate for the modification
Angle grinder with cutting and flap discs, or a saw; clamps and a flat bench or table
MMAW or GMAW welding set and filler to suit
Tape measure, square, straight edge, spirit level
Zinc-rich or other primer the Centre uses, brushes, and the data sheet and SDS
photos: The frame before work, with the damage and the measured diagonals recorded
The group's job plan with tasks and welding order
The cut lines marked and the frame supported
The new member tacked in, with a square or tape checking the diagonals
The modification parts fitted to the marked-up drawing
The finished, primed frame with its final measurements

checklist: Measured and recorded the frame before work
Helped plan cut lines, joint preparation and welding order
Marked and cut out only the damaged member, with the frame supported
Fitted and tacked the new member and checked square and flat before welding
Made and fitted the modification parts to the drawing
Welded in the planned order and corrected any distortion
Cleaned the welds and primed the repaired areas as the data sheet says
Marked up the drawing as built and left the area clean
safety: Check guards and disc ratings before grinding or cutting; wear a face shield and hearing protection
Support the frame so nothing falls or springs when a member is cut out
Weld only behind screens, with extraction, and keep paint and solvents away from hot work
Prime only in a ventilated area, with the gloves and eye protection the SDS names
Treat cut and welded parts as hot and mark them HOT
